title: Contribute
text:
How to contribute a workshop
This catalog is generated from GitHub metadata. To make sure your workshop appears on the Workshops page, follow the rules below.

For workshops in the C3G GitHub organization

Create the repository in the c3g organization.
Name the repository with the c3gW prefix (example: c3gW-intro-rnaseq).
Add the GitHub topic workshop (required).
Add a clear description and, if available, a homepage URL.
Add one or more category topics (recommended), such as:

rna-seq
chip-seq
metagenomics
variant-calling
single-cell
epigenomics
proteomics
genome-assembly
clinical
cancer


If the repository name starts with c3gW and includes the workshop topic, it will be included automatically in the main workshop catalog.


For partner workshops outside the C3G organization
Partner repositories are managed manually.

Open scripts/fetch_workshops_data.py.
Add the repository (owner/repo) to MANUAL_PARTNER_REPO_LIST.
Ensure topics include workshop.
If needed, add or override partner topics in MANUAL_PARTNER_TOPIC_OVERRIDES.

title: Contribute
text:
How to contribute a tutorial
Tutorials are indexed from directories in the c3g/c3gW-Tutorials repository.

Create a new top-level tutorial directory in c3g/c3gW-Tutorials.
Add a README.md inside that directory with these sections:

## Description: brief summary of the tutorial content.
## Tags: topic tags (for example rna-seq, single-cell, variant-calling).

Open a pull request in c3g/c3gW-Tutorials and request review.

Notes:

The tutorial catalog automatically adds the tutorial topic to each directory entry.
Tags from the ## Tags section are normalized to lowercase and shown as tutorial filters in this site.
If a directory is missing README.md metadata, a fallback description is used.


Refresh the catalog data
After adding or updating workshop repositories or tutorial directories:

Run:

python3 scripts/fetch_workshops_data.py

Rebuild the site so the updated data is published.

Tip: you can also enable the commented pre-render step in _quarto.yml to refresh workshop data automatically during site builds.
